subtopic: Deciding whether to quit or persist
subtype: Approach: line up an exit plan before leaving [Action]
passage:
Maria: Signed the offer. Handing in my notice on Friday
Gautam: Wait, I thought you hated the place. Why not quit months ago?
Maria: Because I wanted to do it properly. Updated my CV in March. Saved three months of expenses. Started interviewing in April, always after work
Gautam: And your manager knows?
Maria: Not until this Friday. I'll give a proper handover and finish the report I'm on
Gautam: So you're leaving on good terms
Maria: Yes. No drama. If the new job hadn't come through, I'd still have a safety net 🙂
Gautam: Smart. Let's celebrate on Saturday 🎉

qa.q: What was Maria feeling about handing in the notice?
qa.a: Maria was calm and pleased, having prepared carefully, and glad to leave without any drama.

qa.q: What could Maria do to keep the good terms after handing in the notice, and why?
qa.a: Maria could write a clear handover note and thank the team, because the reputation left behind helps in later references.

qa.q: How does Gautam see Maria's decision to wait before leaving?
qa.a: Gautam at first wondered why Maria had not quit earlier, but now sees that waiting to be ready made the exit safer.

grounding: The person updates the CV, saves three months of expenses and interviews while employed, then resigns on good terms.

subtopic: Deciding whether to quit or persist
subtype: Approach: line up an exit plan before leaving [Action]
passage:
Parveen had worked at the cooperative sugar mill's office in their kasba for two years, counting cane receipts in a room with a slow fan. She wanted out, to the accounts job at the district bank, but she did not walk in and quit.
First, on Sunday evenings, she updated her CV at the cyber cafe beside the bus stand, adding the new billing software she'd learned. Second, she put aside part of each month's pay in a separate account until she had enough to cover a few months of her share of the household costs. Third, she asked Dhruv, her colleague who'd left last year, how he had prepared for the bank's interview, and took two leave days for interviews.
In October the offer came. She handed in her notice with a month's warning, trained her replacement, and her manager gave her a letter of thanks.

qa.q: Where did Parveen update her CV?
qa.a: At the cyber cafe beside the bus stand.

qa.q: How can you tell Parveen felt careful rather than rushed about leaving?
qa.a: She felt determined but cautious, wanting out yet choosing not to walk in and quit before an offer was ready.

qa.q: What else could Parveen do if the first bank interview had failed?
qa.a: She could ask the bank for feedback and keep applying while still at the mill, since staying employed meant she could keep trying without pressure.

qa.q: How does Parveen's exit look to her manager?
qa.a: The manager gets a month's warning and a trained replacement, which is likely why a letter of thanks followed.

grounding: Shows the person updating the CV, saving for a cushion and interviewing while still employed, then leaving on good terms.

subtopic: Deciding whether to quit or persist
subtype: Approach: line up an exit plan before leaving [Action]
passage:
Nadia had spent a year on the customer phones at a Manchester energy company and knew it was time to move on. She also knew what happened to her friend Liam, who'd walked out in a rage and spent the summer panicking.
So she planned. In January she rewrote her CV one evening at a time, adding the training course she'd led for new starters. From February she moved a set amount into savings every payday until she had a buffer she and her flatmate agreed felt safe. In March she started applying, taking interviews on her lunch breaks and one afternoon of annual leave.
The offer came in May, from a council housing office. She told her team leader first, in person, gave the full notice period, and wrote handover notes for every open case.
Her team leader said, "Come back and visit." She did, twice.

qa.q: What might Nadia have been worried about, remembering Liam?
qa.a: She may have been anxious about ending up like Liam, who walked out in a rage and spent the summer panicking.

qa.q: What else could Nadia do to make the next move smooth?
qa.a: She could ask her new employer about the start date and training early, so the handover and the new role do not overlap badly.

qa.q: How does the team leader see Nadia's departure?
qa.a: The team leader is warm about it, saying 'Come back and visit', because Nadia gave full notice and clear handover notes.

grounding: Shows the person preparing a CV, building a savings buffer and interviewing while still employed, then resigning on good terms.
